csv_project_name: DBOM for Electric Vehicle fast charging stations
csv_scope_of_work: MnDOT s Office of Sustainability and Public Health received funding from the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Program to administer fast charging (DCFC) networks at an additional 74 location clusters on roadways outside the alternative fuel corridors. OSPH is using a grant process for procurement with third party entities to own, design, construct, operate and maintain Electric Vehicle fast charging stations that are not within MnDOT s right-of-way.
csv_disciplines_requested: Design Build/Developer, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Structural Engineering

title: DBOM for Electric Vehicle Fast Charging Stations
short_description: Design-build-operate-maintain procurement for 74 electric vehicle fast-charging station clusters in Minnesota.
project_location: Saint Paul, Minnesota, USA; 74 location clusters on roadways outside alternative fuel corridors in Minnesota.
project_scope: Grant-based DBOM procurement for third-party entities to own, design, construct, operate, and maintain direct-current fast-charging (DCFC) stations at an additional 74 location clusters outside MnDOT right-of-way. The project is funded through the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Program. No detailed structural dimensions or building areas are stated.
services: Design-build-operate-maintain developer services, including civil engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, and structural engineering for EV fast-charging stations.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily an EV charging infrastructure program, not a bridge, long-span roof, stadium, or special structural project.
- Structural engineering is listed, but the likely structural scope appears secondary to electrical and site infrastructure.
- No indication of architecturally demanding, lightweight, or complex load-bearing structures.
- DBOM format may include some planning opportunity, but the technical focus is outside sbp's core priorities.
- Distributed multi-site infrastructure program rather than a distinct high-profile structural project.

fee_explanation: No explicit planning fee is stated. The notice is a DBOM/grant procurement for third-party entities and does not provide a separate design fee.
